parsed.mechanism: Microbial or chemical action selectively degrades the cementing compounds binding bast fibers, which causes a directed local increase in configurational entropy as a rigid, low-disorder bound state transforms into many separable arrangements; an LLM training objective can analogously induce targeted 'representational retting' that dissolves entangled superposed features by raising local entropy only at the binding sites, routing previously fused circuits into isolable monosemantic components.
parsed.transfer: From A transfers the principle that entropy quantifies the number of accessible arrangements, applied to B's selective degradation of binding agents — reframing feature disentanglement as a locally entropy-increasing dissolution of the 'cement' that fuses polysemantic representations.
parsed.open_problem: Can a contrastive or sparsity objective be designed to selectively raise configurational entropy only at the binding sites between superposed features, dissolving polysemantic 'cement' while leaving the fibers (monosemantic features) structurally intact and recoverable?
parsed.niche_name: Representational Retting: Entropy-Targeted Dissolution of Polysemantic Feature Binding
parsed.primary_quote: degradating the cementing compounds that bind the bast fibres to other plant tissues, allowing the fibers to be isolated

reasoning_trace.inputs_seen: A: entropy counts the number of arrangements/disorder of a system, monotonic with accessible microstates. B: retting separates fibers by microbial/chemical degradation of the cementing compounds that bind bast fibers to surrounding tissue, isolating the fibers.
reasoning_trace.reasoning: I tried to transfer A's entropy-as-arrangement-count mechanism onto B's selective-dissolution-of-binder mechanism, treating disentanglement of superposed neural features as a retting process: the 'cement' is the correlational binding fusing polysemantic features, and breaking it is a local entropy increase that unlocks many separable configurations. I rejected the naive transfer 'maximize global entropy = better representations' (already trivial/wrong — that just adds noise) and rejected a pure vocabulary match ('disorder = randomness'). The non-trivial core is the SELECTIVITY operator: retting raises entropy ONLY at the binder, not the fiber, so the move is spatially/structurally targeted entropy injection — which maps to a concrete loss that increases configurational entropy at feature-binding sites while preserving feature integrity, a constraint absent from standard disentanglement objectives.
reasoning_trace.decision: Settled on 'representational retting' — an entropy-targeted, binding-site-localized dissolution objective for feature disentanglement — because it gives a falsifiable training-objective design rather than a metaphor.
reasoning_trace.confidence: medium - the selectivity reframing is concrete and testable, but operationalizing 'binding-site-local entropy' precisely is unproven.
reasoning_trace.could_be_wrong_if: If 'raise entropy at binding sites' reduces on inspection to existing sparse-autoencoder/disentanglement regularizers (L1/total-correlation penalties), then the merge is just a vocabulary relabel of known methods rather than a new mechanism.
